'''Cheryl Y. Hayashi''' is a [[biologist]] who specializes in the evolution and functional properties of [[spider silk]]. She is the Provost and Sr. Vice President for Science at the [[American Museum of Natural History]], where she is a curator and professor in the Division of Invertebrate Zoology.  She also serves as the Leon Hess Director of Comparative Biology Research.<ref name="AMNH">{{cite web|title=Staff Profiles: Cheryl Y. Hayashi|url=http://www.amnh.org/our-research/staff-directory/cheryl-y.-hayashi/|access-date=16 February 2024|website=American Museum of Natural History|publisher=American Museum of Natural History}}</ref> She was a graduate of [[Yale University]], a professor at [[University California Riverside]],<ref name="Riverside">{{cite web|title=Cheryl Hayashi|url=http://www.biology.ucr.edu/people/faculty/Hayashi.html|website=Biology UC Riverside|publisher=University of California Riverside|access-date=24 March 2017}}</ref> and a 2007 [[MacArthur Fellows Program|MacArthur Fellow]].<ref name="MacArthur">{{cite web|title=Cheryl Hayashi: Spider Silk Biologist|url=https://www.macfound.org/fellows/828/|website=MacArthur Fellows|publisher=MacArthur Foundation|access-date=24 March 2017|date=28 January 2007}}</ref>

==Education==
Hayashi graduated from [[Iolani High School]] in 1985 and was a member of the school's first co-educational class. She continued her studies at [[Yale University]], gaining a Bachelor of Science in 1988, Master of Science in 1990, and a Master of Philosophy in 1993.<ref name="AMNH" /> She worked with Prof. Catherine Craig, including field work in Panama,<ref name="Yale alumnus profile">{{cite web|last1=Meserole|first1=Rachel|date=26 February 2009|title=Alumnus Profile: Cheryl Hayashi SM '88: "From Science Hill to Spider Silk Studies"|url=https://www.yalescientific.org/2009/02/almunus-profile-cheryl-hayashi-sm-88-from-science-hill-to-spider-silk-studies/|access-date=24 March 2017|website=Yale Scientific|publisher=Yale University}}</ref> becoming interested in spiders when she had the job of hand-feeding the professor's colony of tropical spiders.<ref name="NSF">{{cite web|title=Unraveling the wonders of spider silk|url=https://www.nsf.gov/discoveries/disc_summ.jsp?cntn_id=112760|website=National Science Foundation Discoveries|publisher=National Science Foundation|access-date=24 March 2017|date=9 December 2008}}</ref>

She was awarded a PhD by Yale in 1996, with a dissertation on the [[systematics]] of spiders using [[ribosomal DNA]].<ref name="Hayashi PhD">{{cite book|last1=Hayashi|first1=Cheryl|title=Molecular systematics of spiders: Evidence from ribosomal DNA|date=1996|publisher=Yale University|pages=414 pages|edition=Thesis 9635417}}</ref>

==Career==
After working as a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Wyoming (1996-2001),<ref name="MacArthur" /> Hayashi was a professor at [[University of California, Riverside|UC Riverside]] from 2001 to the end of 2016.<ref name="Riverside" />

Her UC Riverside laboratory's work characterized spiders in the [[spidroin]] gene family, including how silk is encoded and studying the basis of molecular diversity in spiders. A variety of techniques, including whole-gene cloning, [[genomics]], [[biochemistry]], and [[biomechanics]], were used to study the evolution of spider silk.<ref name="Riverside" /> Hayashi worked with engineers and biomechanics to understand spider silk, and to develop [[biomaterials]] based on spider genetic information.<ref name="Riverside" />

She became curator, professor, and Leon Hess Director of Comparative Biology Research at the [[American Museum of Natural History]] in January 2017, where she initially served as the Director of the Institute for Comparative Genomics.  She was appointed Provost and Sr. VP for Science in 2021.<ref name="AMNH" />

Hayashi was a speaker at the TED 2010 Conference.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://conferences.ted.com/TED2010/program/speakers.php|title=TED2010: Speakers A-Z|website=conferences.ted.com|access-date=2010-03-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110713095454/http://conferences.ted.com/TED2010/program/speakers.php|archive-date=2011-07-13|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://blog.ted.com/2010/02/discovery_round.php|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100213220038/http://blog.ted.com/2010/02/discovery_round.php|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 13, 2010|title=Discovery: Roundup of TED2010, Session 2|date=11 February 2010|website=ted.com}}</ref>

==Awards==
She was the recipient of the [[MacArthur Fellowship Program]] in 2007.<ref name="MacArthur" />
